svg.text: Hinting a stored key: at most two cache-line hints
Before a compare, a task hints the first bytes of the key it will read. A key block of 2 KiB is 32 cache lines of 64 B; its first 24 B are the header. The hint covers
the line holding the first requested bytes and at most one more. When those lines fit in the record’s first block, addresses are computed directly; otherwise
the reference is validated, the header is read for the link and the continuation line is hinted. Comparisons skip header bytes; a long key can still miss.
Fast path: the hinted lines fit in the first block
RangeRef: first block A · offset 600 · begin 48 B · blockGen 9
key block A
begin bytes 600..647: line 9 and 8 B of line 10, both inside A
header 24 B
line 8
line 16
line 24
line 31
address = A + 600; line 9 holds bytes 576..639 of A, so the begin starts 24 B into it and its last 8 B fall in line 10. Two hints from the computed addresses; no header read,
no link followed. The validity of A’s generation is not consulted on this path: the hint is only a hint, and the compare that follows is guarded by the CV check made earlier.
Linked path: the first requested bytes end the block
RangeRef: first block A · offset 2016 · begin 48 B · blockGen 9
key block A
record starts at byte 2016: the last 32 B of line 31
header 24 B
line 8
line 16
line 24
line 31
key block B (A.nextBlock)
the record continues after B’s header: bytes 24..39 of line 0, then on
header 24 B
line 8
line 16
line 24
line 31
nextBlock, read from A’s header
header bytes: inside the hinted line, skipped by the comparison
validity first: blockGen 9 > lastReclaimedKeyGeneration? If not, the reference is stale and nothing is read (Figure 4).
the requested bytes do not fit in A after offset 2016, so A’s header is read for nextBlock. This read is a demand access, not a hint.
two hints: A’s line 31, which holds the first 32 B, and B’s line 0, where the record resumes right after the 24 B header.
nothing beyond those two lines is hinted. A key longer than what they hold, or a long key compared to its end, can still take demand misses.
record bytes requested by the compare
rest of the record (end key): outside the requested begin; may share a hinted line
cache line hinted (prefetch)
key-block header, 24 B
What the hint is, and what it is not
A hint is a prefetch for a later visit: it does not copy the record, does not guarantee the lines are still cached when the compare runs, and is never issued
for a reference whose generation has not passed the validity test on the linked path. The two-hint limit bounds prefetch issuance; locating a key in
later blocks can still require several header reads. Keys that do not fit are compared with ordinary loads, where the remaining demand misses come from.
External input keys (the reads’ own begins) get the same treatment: at most two cache-line hints from their addresses.
